Hi Tom,

Thanks for the feedback.

I've extended experi() to handle ada, and that is now updated on http://onepager.togaware.com/ (Models).

However I can't seem to repeat the problem you are having - perhaps try the following and see if you get the error - also note that control with rpart.control does not yet work.

library(rpart)
library(randomForest)
library(ada)

weather <- read.csv("http://rattle.togaware.com/weather.csv")
ds      <- weather
target  <- "RainTomorrow"
vars    <- colnames(ds)
risk    <- "RISK_MM"
ignore  <- vars[c(1, 2, ifelse(exists("risk"), which(risk==vars), NULL))]
vars    <- setdiff(vars, ignore)
form    <- formula(paste(target, "~ ."))

source("http://onepager.togaware.com/experi.R")

ex.rp <- experi(form, ds[vars], target, "rpart", "1", n=10,
                keep.pr <http://keep.pr>=TRUE)

ex.rf <- experi(form, ds[vars], target, "randomForest", "500", n=10,
                control=list(na.action=na.omit), keep.pr <http://keep.pr>=TRUE)

ex.ad <http://ex.ad> <- experi(form, ds[vars], target, "ada", "50", n=10,
                keep.pr <http://keep.pr>=TRUE)

(results <- rbind(ex.rp, ex.rf, ex.ad <http://ex.ad>))

Regards,
Graham

Thanks Tom.

I could not get the same error you did, but did get different errors:

1) The target is numeric so without knowing experi() just does a regression rather than a classification.

2) The dataset is small and experi does rather trivial sampling, so it can generate a test dataset with no cases in it. Experi() now checks for that.

With current version of experi(), the following works:

library(randomForest)
library(ada)

sample <- read.csv("sample.csv")

ds      <- sample
target  <-"WashOutIND"
vars    <- colnames(ds)
risk    <- "Null"
ignore  <- vars[c(1, 2, ifelse(exists("risk"), which(risk==vars), NULL))]
vars    <- setdiff(vars, ignore)

ds[[target]] <- as.factor(ds[[target]])

form    <- formula(paste(target, "~ ."))
source("http://onepager.togaware.com/experi.R")
ex.rp <- experi(form,ds[vars], target, "rpart", "1", n=10,
                keep.pr <http://keep.pr>=TRUE)

#ex.rf <- experi(form, ds[vars], target, "randomForest", "500", n=10,
 #               control=list(na.action=na.omit), keep.pr <http://keep.pr>=TRUE)

ex.ad <http://ex.ad> <- experi(form, ds[vars], target, "ada", "50", n=10,
                 keep.pr <http://keep.pr>=TRUE)

(results <- rbind(ex.rp, ex.ad <http://ex.ad>))

RGtk2 is a rather key dependency for Rattle. Have you tried installing it from the R console rather than from within RStudio. I have seen that RStudio does some extra work with libraries and paths on starting up - and I wonder if somehow that interferes with the install of RGtk2 (or with the underlying GTK+ zip file that is separately downloaded and installed for you as part of the install).

You could also try installing GTK+ manually, unzipping the downloaded GTK+ zip file and adding the location to the PATH variable.

Graham Williams

On 26 January 2013 15:17, William Kong <wwko...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi there,
>
> I recently updated my version of rattle directly from the Togaware repo to 2.6.25 but now I'm having issues with the plot builder. Specifically, it won't read any .csv files that are loaded into rattle as data. Is anyone else having this issue?

Hi William,

Thanks for reporting the issue.

To have Plot Builder find the Rattle dataset I was assigning it temporarily to a variable in the Global Environment. The CRAN policy (http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/policies.html) notes that "Packages should not modify the global environment" - rattle could potentially wipe out a dataset in the Global Environment if it had the same name.

CRAN (Ripley) suggested that Rattle would not be updated on CRAN unless it complied with Policy. So I've removed the assignment until I identify a better solution.

One work-around is to do the following yourself (which is what Rattle was automatically doing) in the R Console just prior to clicking the Execute button in Rattle to start up Plot Builder:

> ds <- crs$dataset

Plot Builder will then see the dataset.

I've also temporarily re-enabled this in the 2.6.26 beta available now on Togaware:

> install.packages("rattle", repo="http://rattle.togaware.com")

Plot Builder is such a great tool - I'll try and work out another solution that conforms to CRAN policy to have it work seamlessly with Rattle.

Graham Williams
http://togaware.com

messages.subject: Re: kmeans within Rattle does not "see" numeric variable?
messages.subject_clean: kmeans within Rattle does not "see" numeric variable?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Many thanks to Graham Williams for passing a tip to me that enabled me to answer my own question.

The error arose because I misunderstood the relationship between target versus input variables on the one hand  and clustering on the other hand. I assumed that kmeans will perform clustering on the target variable. In my case, I designated y as the target variable. Variable y was coded as numeric variable, so I could not understand why rattle refused to handle it.

But instead rattle tried to perform kmeans clustering on the input variables. In my case, the two input variables (factor1 and factor2) are both coded as factors (despite the fact that the values stored in them are integers that got coded as factors "1", "2", etc.) So rattle choked. When I converted factor1 and factor2 to integers, the clustering worked without complaint. However, if I want to perform clustering on the target variable instead of the input variables, I have to use kmeans directly (as opposed to via rattle interface.)

YKE
